changelog.p.002: A concise record of every public PickVia release. Download the latest version from GitHub.
changelog.p.003: Choose more browsers and editions, with Firefox profiles grouped by their associated edition.
changelog.li.001: Add Chrome Dev and Canary; Edge Beta, Dev, and Canary; Brave Beta and Nightly; Vivaldi Snapshot; and Firefox Developer Edition and Nightly as separate browser choices.
changelog.li.002: Add normal app-level routing for Opera, Arc, Orion, and Safari Technology Preview.
changelog.li.003: Keep Firefox profiles with their recorded edition when it can be identified, and remove old detected duplicates when rescanning. Profiles without reliable association metadata retain the existing fallback.
changelog.li.004: Fix Firefox profile paths that were rejected after macOS temporary-path normalization.
changelog.li.005: Show only supported route combinations. Private windows remain browser-level choices; profile-specific private mode is unavailable.
changelog.p.004: DuckDuckGo is now available as a browser choice, with a private option on supported official builds.
changelog.li.006: Choose ordinary or private DuckDuckGo from the same chooser.
changelog.li.007: Private mode uses isolated disposable state, needs no extension or Accessibility permission, and is limited to supported official direct-download builds.
changelog.p.005: Google Chrome Beta is now a separate browser choice, with its own profiles and normal or private options.
changelog.p.006: Email links can now open in the installed mail app you choose.
changelog.li.008: Pick from registered mail apps and manage their order in Mail Settings.
changelog.li.009: PickVia does not preview or save recipients, subjects, message bodies, or the original mail link.
changelog.p.007: The first public release: choose a browser, profile, or supported private mode for each web link.
changelog.li.010: Support Safari, Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, and Firefox.

changelog.description.001: Release notes for PickVia, the native macOS link chooser.
index.title.001: PickVia - Choose the right browser or profile for each web link
index.p.001: Available in 80 app and website languages, with 12 README translations. Choose your language in Settings.
index.p.002: A native link chooser for macOS
index.h1.001:
Stop opening
links in the
wrong browser or profile.
index.p.003: PickVia asks before each web or email link opens, so web links go to the browser or profile you choose and mail links go to the email app you intended.
index.div.001: Download v1.5 ↓★ Star on GitHub
index.p.004: macOS 14+ · Apple Silicon · Free & open source
index.p.007: Choose the destination that fits each web or email link.
index.p.008: Choose an enabled browser or profile, or a supported browser-level private window.
index.p.009: Choose the registered mail app you want instead of sending every mailto: link to the same default.
index.p.010: Put your usual choices in order, then use one click or a keyboard shortcut.
index.p.011: Choose separate Chrome and Edge editions, Brave Beta or Nightly, Vivaldi Snapshot, and Firefox Developer Edition or Nightly. Firefox profiles with a known edition association stay with that edition.
index.p.012: Opera, Arc, Orion, and Safari Technology Preview offer normal browser choices. Profile and private-window support varies by browser. See browser support →
index.p.014: macOS normally sends mailto: links to one default app. PickVia lets you choose among the registered mail apps on your Mac each time.
index.div.002: PRIVATE BY DESIGNPickVia routes the original request directly to your choice. It does not log or persist mail content.
index.p.016: Configure your usual browser profiles and mail apps once, then reorder the targets you use most.
index.h2.004:
Open the next link
in the right place.

privacy.p.003: PickVia does not collect, transmit, sell, or share personal data. The app has no accounts, analytics, advertising, or telemetry.
privacy.li.001: Links are handled locally and passed directly to the browser or mail app you choose.
privacy.li.002: PickVia does not log or retain opened URLs, recipients, subjects, or message bodies.
privacy.li.003: Settings are stored locally in your Application Support folder.
privacy.li.004: When you grant browser-profile access, PickVia stores a local security-scoped bookmark and reads only the metadata needed to identify profiles. It does not read browsing history, cookies, sessions, saved passwords, or page content.
privacy.p.004: The PickVia website does not use analytics, advertising trackers, forms, or cookies set by PickVia. It is hosted by GitHub Pages. GitHub may process technical request information under its Privacy Statement.
privacy.p.005: Browsers, mail apps, GitHub, and other services you choose to open or visit have their own privacy practices. PickVia does not control those services.
privacy.p.006: If this policy changes, the updated version and effective date will be published on this page.
privacy.p.007: Questions about privacy can be sent to bozhenpeng93@gmail.com.
terms.p.003: PickVia is a free, open-source macOS application. You may use, copy, modify, and distribute it under the MIT License included with the project.
terms.p.004: PickVia does not require an account, subscription, or payment. Downloads are provided through the project's official GitHub releases.
terms.p.005: You are responsible for deciding whether to install and use PickVia, choosing which applications receive your links, keeping your Mac secure, and complying with applicable laws. Only bypass macOS Gatekeeper protections when you trust the downloaded release.
terms.p.006: PickVia is provided "as is," without warranties or guarantees of any kind. To the extent permitted by law, the developer is not liable for damages or losses arising from use of, or inability to use, PickVia.
terms.p.007: PickVia can open third-party browsers, mail apps, websites, and services. Those products are governed by their own terms and are not controlled or endorsed by PickVia.
terms.p.008: PickVia may be updated, changed, or discontinued at any time. These terms may also be updated, with the new version and effective date published here.
terms.p.009: Questions about these terms can be sent to bozhenpeng93@gmail.com.

release.v1_5.safari: Try experimental Safari Stable profiles with Accessibility and Automation permissions. Each link opens in a new window of the selected profile.
release.v1_5.duckduckgo: Simplify DuckDuckGo private-session recovery and cleanup. Compatible unsandboxed 1.203.x builds support private routing; normal links have no version or publisher-signature requirement.
release.v1_5.signing: Use a fixed Apple Development certificate for builds. The download is not notarized; follow the README installation instructions.
